data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The preference for better-corroborated theories inevitably smuggles in induction, rendering Popper's position internally inconsistent when moving from logic to action.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If Popper can ground the preference in a non-inductive principle like 'minimize known error' without assuming future success.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the concept of 'rational action' can be decoupled from expectations of future performance.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"To prefer theory A over B because A has survived tests while B has not (or fewer) implies an expectation that A will continue to succeed where B might fail.
